    About the charts

    Cash: 6-max, 100bb deep. Opens are 2.5bb; the small blind opens to 3bb and plays raise-or-fold. 3-bets go to 7.5bb in position and 10bb from the blinds, 4-bets to 20 to 22bb, squeezes to 11 to 13bb, and raises over limpers to 4bb plus 1bb per limper, 1bb more from the small blind (3.5bb from the big blind against a small blind limp). These charts are solver-style approximations rounded to simple frequencies. You can edit any of them in Charts.

    Full ring: 8 players with the same sizes. Opens from UTG and UTG+1 are tighter; from the lojack on, opens and big blind defense match the 6-max seat with the same number of players left to act.

    Live: 8 players. Big opens are 5bb with 150bb stacks; 3-bets go to 15bb in position and 20bb from the blinds. Straddled pots have a 2bb straddle under the gun and 100bb stacks; opens go to 6bb (7bb from the small blind) and the straddler 3-bets to 22bb. Deep spots are 200bb with 2.5bb opens; 3-bets go to 9bb in position and 12bb from the blinds, and 4-bets to 25 to 28bb. These are hand-built approximations adjusted from the standard charts, and each one can outline what changed.

    MTT: 8-max with a 1bb big blind ante, chip EV, equal stacks. Shove, call-a-shove and 3-bet jam spots come from an equilibrium solver run on real all-in equities, and grading uses each hand's EV in big blinds. Open and big blind defense charts at 20 to 40bb are hand-built approximations graded by frequency.

    ICM: bubble spots from a $10, 8-player sit & go ($40 / $24 / $16) and final-table spots with 6 left, solved with prize money instead of chips. EV is shown in dollars and graded by converting to big blinds at your stack's ICM value. Heads-up: classic push/fold, no ante.

    All push/fold solutions assume at most one caller, the usual simplification for these charts. Play: opponents read your betting over the session and adjust.

    Postflop drills: c-bet, turn barrel, check-raise and multiway answers follow the patterns solvers show, worked out from each board's range math, so treat them as guidelines. Check-raise calls are graded on equity against the bets, and multiway spots show your equity against both players. River bets and facing-a-bet answers are exact math under the stated player types: how often each type calls, and what it bets with.

    Sessions, hands and coaching plans save privately to your Claude account when you open Preflop Lab in Claude, and on this device otherwise. Claude reviews, plans and the coach chat use your own Claude usage.

    On a keyboard: F, C, R and A (all-in) to act, Enter for the next hand. In odds drills, 1 to 4 pick an answer, or C and F to call or fold.
